finding.shortLabel: Ann/Gilman as a Gurney instance on the Norfolk corridor

sources.locator: vol. 2 (1805), p. 445: Hingham parish and the Gurney manorial holding ('Hingham Gurneys').

finding.statement: The Ann Gurney x John Gilman marriage threads a Gurney-surname connection through the same Norfolk-to-New-England corridor that received John. It took place at Hingham, Norfolk - ancient Gurney manorial territory (the manor of Hingham Gurneys) and one of the parishes that fed the Norfolk cohort settling Hingham, Massachusetts - into a Norfolk worsted-weaving family, and the couple's son emigrated to New England. Whether or not Ann was John's own sister (an open question), the connection is a concrete Gurney instance on the corridor; if the sisterhood holds, it places a second Gurney sibling on the Norfolk-to-New-England route, reinforcing the corridor reading of a Norfolk origin. The origin conclusion itself is held to the identity work.

finding.shortLabel: Ann Gurney x John Gilman, Hingham Norfolk 1626

sources.locator: pp. 155-160: Gilman family - John Gilman worsted weaver, children baptised West Dereham and Hingham, and John Gilman Jr.'s emigration to Exeter, New Hampshire.
Hingham, Norfolk, parish register: marriage of Ann Gurney and John Gilman, 1 October 1626; burial of Ann Gurney (Gilman), 23 November 1651 (Norfolk Record Office; accessed via Ancestry).

finding.statement: Ann Gurney married John Gilman, a worsted weaver, at Hingham, Norfolk, on 1 October 1626; the couple's children were baptised at West Dereham and Hingham, Ann was buried at Hingham on 23 November 1651, and their son John Gilman Jr. later emigrated to Exeter, New Hampshire. West Dereham, in western Norfolk near Downham Market, lies about twenty miles from the East Dereham parish of Francis Gurney's children.

sources.locator: West Dereham, Norfolk, marriage of Ann Gurney and Peter Woodcocke, 8 February 1618/19 (NRO PD 192/2; FreeREG index) - a separately recorded Ann Gurney who may be a distinct person.
'Gurney family genealogy' (Pennyghael, 2021): Ann identified as a daughter of Francis Gurney by his first marriage. Compiled genealogy, not a record.

finding.statement: Whether the Ann Gurney who married John Gilman at Hingham in 1626 was John Gurney's sister is unresolved. The Pease genealogy identifies her as a daughter of Francis Gurney by his first marriage - which, if correct, would make her John's sister - but no primary record links her to Francis, her Gilman children were baptised at West Dereham some twenty miles from Francis's East Dereham parish, and a separately recorded Ann Gurney married Peter Woodcocke at West Dereham in 1618/19 and may be a different woman. The kinship rests on a single compiled genealogy, not a record.
